reproduces: R2 missing-plugin (runs/2026-09-12-q42-review/results.json): the baseline navmesh entry came back `reused` after its consumed plugin was deleted, because changed_input read `exists() and hash differs` so absence was `no change`
registry: fixture-check-registry.json (the existing trim; this case needs no extra check)
note: Every step drives the CLI on ONE run directory that was fully run first. The generated fixture tree is restored after each damage step, in a finally block, so a later case never runs against a damaged fixture.

steps.damage: delete the generated FixtureTarget.esp (a plugin every geometry receipt consumed)

invalidatedByName.rule: D5b: a consumed plugin GONE or changed at its recorded path is a change, named with the path. D5's transitive rule then carries it to reverse, diff and the derived order evaluation.

steps.detailNextActionRule: D5: every transition names the reason and, in the ledger entry's detail, the next action (re-run, re-plan, restore the file)

afterRerunAndFinalize.why: with the file gone the fake writes a zero sha256 for it, and D2(c) rejects an emit that consumed a request plugin at another hash, so the re-run cannot restore a completed claim

steps.damage: append bytes to candidate-01-reorder.json after the run (only that arm's input)

invalidatedByName.rulingApplied: A-6 as corrected by A-7: the PART entries (__arm, __reverse, __diff) rest at invalidated(the candidate file ... changed on disk ...) - the truthful reason - and the launch refusal is written as the PART-LESS accounting entry, the shape Q42's blocked(candidate-missing) already had. So blocked(candidate-changed) is asserted on the accounting entry and the invalidated transition stays asserted on the part.
invalidatedByName.rule: D5b: the candidate file gone or changed, named with the path

steps.damage: blank one consumed plugin's sha256 inside an ACCEPTED receipt on disk (geometry.navmesh-ownership__baseline__arm, plugin FixtureTarget.esp)

expect.rule: D5a: any consumed plugin without a path or a 64-hex hash is a GAP (unverifiable), so the entry is refused-reuse(<gap>) — not reused (a silent certainty) and not invalidated (a change nobody measured)

steps.damage: null the recorded baseEmitSha256 inside an ACCEPTED candidate-arm receipt on disk (geometry.navmesh-ownership__candidate-01-reorder__arm), leaving baseEmitPath in place

expect.rule: A-9 (V's finding 2): a run-internal comparison input recorded without a hash is unverifiable, so reuse refuses it — the same answer finalize's integrity walk gives for that receipt, never a silent grant on one verb and a refusal on the other

steps.damage: none: a second resume over a run nothing has touched

expect.rule: D5: else `reused`. Zero children is the measurement that reuse actually happened.

steps.damage: delete the generated FixtureTarget.esp and call `run` (not `resume`)

invalidatedByName.rule: D5: `A run over a ledger with terminal-ok entries performs the same revalidation resume does; no verb reuses without it.` There is no verb difference.

steps.damage: append a byte to the scope file the plan recorded

expect.rule: D5: run, resume and finalize refuse by name when the registry file or the scope file at the plan's recorded path is missing or no longer hashes to the plan (registry-changed, registry-missing, scope-changed, scope-missing), with the next action `re-run scopeprobe and plan again`

steps.rulingApplied: A-3: run/resume refuse a changed or missing registry/scope with exit 2 (`REFUSED: scope-changed: ...` on stderr, no work done); finalize refuses with exit 3 and a refusal disposition. The derived 2 stands, and the stderr prefix is now asserted too.

baseEmitDependency.rule: D4: for check C the candidate `arm` receipt records the baseline `arm` emit of C as its base emit (consumed.baseEmitPath/Sha256); the `reverse` receipt records the candidate `arm` emit; the `diff` receipt records both under consumed.inputs

diffReceipt.rulingApplied: A-4: the diff receipt's consumed.inputs has exactly two rows (part `arm` and part `reverse`, each with path and sha256) and its baseEmitPath/Sha256 stay null; the candidate arm receipt's baseEmit is the baseline arm emit of the same check and the reverse receipt's baseEmit is the candidate arm emit.
